results.title: SEC & FINRA Rules on Automated Trading and Algorithms – Day Trader Business
results.content: SEC rules for automated trading require firms to have robust risk controls, real-time monitoring, and testing of algorithms. Key compliance requirements for algorithmic trading under SEC and FINRA rules include implementing robust supervisory controls, maintaining written policies and procedures, conducting pre-trade risk checks, ensuring proper order-handling practices, and maintaining detailed audit trails. Risk controls for automated trading systems include pre-trade risk checks, real-time monitoring, circuit breakers to halt trading during volatility, order size limits, and algorithm validation procedures as mandated by SEC and FINRA rules. Best practices for algorithm risk management under SEC and FINRA rules include implementing robust testing and validation for algorithms before live trading, establishing real-time monitoring to detect unusual activity, setting strict controls and limits on order placement and execution, maintaining comprehensive audit trails, and ensuring compliance with all regulatory reporting requirements. Automated traders must register with the SEC or FINRA if required, maintain detailed records of trading algorithms, and comply with reporting rules on trade activity, algorithm changes, and risk controls.

results.title: (PDF) Sample, sample size and sampling: a review of current recommendations
results.content: Introduction: The present review is based on the need to know the current recommendations on the sample, sample size and sampling that are considered in various empirical studies, aspects that certainly can generate confusion especially in novice researchers. Results: Current recommendations revolve around performing power analysis to calculate the sample size, regardless of the type of sampling to be used, in addition to the fact that it is a good practice to be guided by the sample sizes of other studies with similar characteristics, preferably from journals indexed in high-level databases. is the appropriate sample size for my research? Sample Size and its Importance in Research. Sample Size for Survey Research: Review and Recommendaons. Approaches to sample size calculation according to study design are presented with examples in health research. For sample size estimation, researchers need to (1) provide information regarding the statistical analysis to be applied, (2) determine acceptable precision levels, (3) decide on study power, (4) specify the confidence level, and (5) determine the magnitude of practical significance differences (effect size). Due to the range of conflicting criteria regarding minimum sample size needed for a scale/questionnaire validation study, the objective of this review is to analyze sample sizes used in published journal articles to contribute a pragmatic perspective to the discussion on sample sizes. This study is limited by its focus on a single database and by including all phases of validation from initial quantitative instrument design studies (which tend to have the lowest sample sizes) up to international macro-studies (which can have hundreds of thousands of participants.) Nevertheless, the results of this study provide an additional practical perspective for the academic discussion regarding minimum sample size based on accepted practice. Sample Size for Survey Research: Review and Recommendations. Although there are several widely adopted rules of thumb to calculate sample size, researchers remain unclear about which one to consider when determining sample size in their respective studies. We hope that this editorial does not only provide researchers a fundamental understanding of sample size and its associated issues, but also facilitates their consideration of sample size determination in their own studies.
